operations.text:
The diagram shows how a recording and reference score become score-linked feedback.
The explanations follow the diagram's module labels.

STAGE 1: USER INPUT
• The user supplies a clarinet recording and its reference score.

STAGE 2: TRANSCRIPTION
• The transcriber estimates note pitches and onset times.
• Postprocessing refines the candidate note sequence.

STAGE 3: ALIGNMENT
• The aligner matches performed notes to written locations.
• It tracks repeated visits to the same passage.

STAGE 3.1: NOTE ERROR LABELLING
• The system identifies wrong, missed and extra notes from the alignment.
• It distinguishes repeated passages from extra notes.

STAGE 3.2: RHYTHM ERROR LABELLING
• The earlier system compares performed and reference timing to identify rhythm errors.

STAGE 4: LABEL OUTPUT
• Each label links an error type to affected notes and a replay interval.

AudioEval links clarinet performance errors to written notes and replay intervals.
The earlier system combines transcription, alignment, note-error and rhythm-error labelling.
Synthetic performances provide known note-to-score relationships for training.
The historical model used 4,544 training recordings and 358 validation recordings.
The current revision uses CTC transcription and bounded passage alignment; its accuracy still needs evaluation.

The paper evaluates earlier AudioEval configurations on synthetic and real recordings.
The comparisons use different metrics and do not evaluate the current revision.

PRACTICAL STRENGTHS
• Score locations and replay intervals make each error easy to review.
• Repeat tracking distinguishes successive attempts at the same passage.

CURRENT METHOD LIMITS
• Repeated phrases, same-pitch attacks and bounded searches can cause failures.
• The current method omits rhythm, intonation and timbre error labels.
• An empty error list does not confirm a clean performance.

STUDY LIMITS
• The revised pipeline still needs a matched evaluation.
• The synthetic set was used during development; 21 recordings overlapped baseline training and 3 overlapped model selection.
• Training data and label coverage differ across systems.
• The real set includes 11 recordings by one player.
• Real scoring includes rhythm errors that the baselines do not predict.

MUSICPAL: PROPOSED DEVICE
• The device would record, display score-linked feedback and replay passages.
• Manually reviewed sessions could support future training and evaluation.

Earlier results support score-linked feedback, while the revised method needs independent evaluation.
Future tests should include more players, pieces and recording conditions.
MusicPal remains a proposed way to present the feedback.

CASE STUDY
• The system linked a return at 9.8 s to bars 1-4 in Howl's Moving Castle.
• It identified C6 instead of A5 in bar 12.
• Human annotations corroborated three repetitions and the discussed wrong note.

operations.alt_text: User-supplied diagram of the earlier AudioEval architecture: Stage 1 user input; Stage 2 transcription and postprocessing; Stage 3 alignment; Stage 3.1 note error labelling; Stage 3.2 rhythm error labelling; Stage 4 label output. The current revision does not emit rhythm-error labels.

Historical AudioEval comparisons with full-sentence bullet captions. Synthetic weighted micro-F1 is 61.04%, versus 41.39% and 34.71%; real error-event micro-F1 is 25.49%, versus 1.96% and 3.20%. The metrics differ and do not assess the revised pipeline.
